notes:
Topline: MidPort is a mid-market SaaS product analytics company (B2B) running in-app agent + document search. Ran Hosted API trial (30 days) and now evaluating Dedicated for predictable latency and cost at scale. Key stakeholders: VP Product (Nadia K.), Head of Infra (Tom S.), Procurement (Jared).

Trial summary (Hosted API)
- Started 2024-10-18, seed traffic: 1k DAU pilot -> expanded to 5k DAU.
- Observed baseline: 14 QPS sustained during business hours, spikes to ~85 QPS in BH events (weekly digest push).
- Token mix observed: avg prompt 70 tokens, avg completion 180 tokens; 60% short chat queries (~<100 tokens total), 25% doc-search/embedding lookups (embedding calls small but frequent), 15% long-form summaries/reranking (avg request ~500 tokens).
- Cost: Hosted API token spend ran ~ $9k/mo during trial (with caching + aggressive client-side dedup). Engineering called this 'manageable but unpredictable' when spikes hit.

POC asks / Dedicated sizing question set (from SE/R&D)
- Primary ask: Draft QPS-to-GPU sizing table with target headroom (1.5x and 2.0x), include expected token throughput per GPU for our model family (Llama-like 70B quantized candidate).
- Target latency SLO: p95 < 250ms for short chat path; p99 < 900ms for long summaries.
- Throughput target: support 120 QPS burst with sustained 30 QPS baseline (concurrency planning: ~40-60 concurrent requests depending on batching).
- Token mix to model: assume 65% short chat, 20% embeddings/rerank, 15% long completions. Need token/sec forecast by peak window and 95th percentile.
- Cost sensitivity: Finance prefers 'predictable monthly commit' vs pay-as-you-go. Looking at 3-6 month reserved capacity options + burst.

Security / Compliance notes
- Require SSO/SAML + SCIM provisioning, audit logs forwarded to Splunk, and KMS integration for key rotation. Data residency: logs must be retained in us-east region.
- Security team completed initial questionnaire (see Drive: security-faq-midport), needs SOC2 Type II report and architecture diagram for Dedicated network boundaries.
